chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Hujr ibn Zaida, from Humran ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): I have given Allah an oath that I will not leave Medina until you inform me of what I ask you. He said to me: Ask. I said: Am I of your Shia? He said: Yes, in this world and the next.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam's confirmation of being 'Shia' in this world and the next?
ai.summary: This narration from *Rijal al-Kashi* highlights the concept of *al-wala'* (loyalty) as a definitive criterion for true Shi'ism, affirmed directly by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to his companion Humran ibn A'yan. The Imam’s declaration that Humran is of their Shia 'in this world and the hereafter' underscores the permanence of this spiritual bond, linking earthly allegiance to eternal salvation in Shia theological discourse.
